senses.definition: A short story, often about animals that act like people, that suggests a lesson.
senses.example: We read a fable about a lion and a mouse.

senses.definition: One flat surface of a solid shape.
senses.example: We counted all six faces of the box.

senses.definition: Something that is true and can be checked.
senses.example: It is a fact that our school has two playgrounds.

senses.definition: A number that multiplies by another number to make a given number.
senses.example: Six is a factor of twelve because six times two is twelve.

senses.definition: To slowly grow weaker, less clear, or less bright.
senses.example: The sound faded as the bus drove away.

senses.definition: To be unable to do what you tried to do, or for something to stop working.
senses.example: I failed to hear the first bell because the room was loud.

senses.definition: Not clear, strong, or easy to notice.
senses.example: I saw a faint line on the old map.

senses.definition: To suddenly pass out for a short time. Fainting is different from falling asleep.
senses.example: The girl felt dizzy and was afraid she might faint.

senses.definition: Treating people by reasonable rules or giving people an appropriate chance.
senses.example: It was fair to let each player have a turn.

senses.definition: An event with things to see, try, buy, or learn about.
senses.example: We saw goats and model trains at the town fair.

senses.definition: Quite light in color, especially of skin or hair.
senses.example: The story described the child as having fair hair.

senses.definition: Acceptable or in the middle on a scale of quality.
senses.example: The used books were sorted into fair, good, and excellent condition.

senses.definition: In sports such as baseball, in or on the part of the field where a hit can count.
senses.example: The ball landed on the line and was called fair.

senses.definition: Strong trust or belief in someone or something.
senses.example: My teacher had faith that I could finish the project.

senses.definition: Religious belief, or a group of beliefs followed by people.
senses.example: Our neighbors practice different faiths.

senses.definition: Made to look real or true though it is not.
senses.example: We used fake coins in the classroom shop.

senses.definition: An object or person that is trying to pass for something they are not.
senses.example: The museum guide showed us how she could tell the picture was a fake.

senses.definition: To pretend to feel or do something that is not real.
senses.example: He tried to fake a sneeze for the play.

senses.definition: To move downward or drop, usually because of gravity.
senses.example: Watch the ripe apples fall from the tree.

senses.definition: The season after summer and before winter.
senses.example: Many leaves change color in the fall.

senses.definition: Known or easy to recognize because you have seen, heard, or used it before.
senses.example: A familiar song began to play.

senses.definition: A group of people connected through birth, marriage, adoption, care, or close ties.
senses.example: My family reads together after dinner.

senses.definition: A group of related things or living things.
senses.example: The house cat and the lion belong to the same animal family.

senses.definition: Known by many people.
senses.example: That bridge is famous for its tall towers.

senses.definition: A person who enjoys and follows a person, team, or activity.
senses.example: My friend is a fan of the local hockey team.

senses.definition: A tool or device that moves air.
senses.example: The fan made the room feel cooler.

senses.definition: To move air toward something or to spread out in a wide shape.
senses.example: The guide fanned out a set of cards on the table.

senses.definition: More decorated, special, or costly than usual.
senses.example: Mila wore a fancy hat with silver stars.

senses.definition: To want, like, or imagine something.
senses.example: Do you fancy a stroll before dinner?

senses.definition: A long way from a place, time, or point.
senses.example: The goal was at the far end of the field.

senses.definition: A long way, or a lot more than something else.
senses.example: The dog ran far ahead of us.

senses.definition: A place where people grow crops, raise animals, or both.
senses.example: We bought carrots at a local farm.

senses.definition: To grow crops or raise animals as work.
senses.example: They farm the flat land near the river.

senses.definition: A style of clothing, hair, or another thing that is popular at a certain time.
senses.example: Wide ties came back into fashion for a while.

senses.definition: To shape or make something, often by hand.
senses.example: We fashioned a handle from a piece of soft wire.

senses.definition: Able to move, happen, or be done quickly.
senses.example: A fast train passed the little station.

senses.definition: At high speed or firmly in place.
senses.example: The rabbit ran fast across the grass.

senses.definition: To choose to eat no food or certain foods for a time, sometimes for religious or medical reasons.
senses.example: Some people fast as part of a religious observance.

senses.definition: Responsibility for something that went wrong, or a flaw in what someone did.
senses.example: I thought the spill was my fault until I saw the cup had a hole.

senses.definition: A break in rock where material on one side has moved next to material on the other.
senses.example: The map shows a fault running through the valley.

senses.definition: To blame someone for something or point out what is wrong with it.
senses.example: I would not fault you for asking a good question.

senses.definition: A helpful thing one person does for another.
senses.example: Can you do me a favor and hand me the paper?

senses.definition: Support for a person, idea, or choice.
senses.example: Most voters were in favor of planting trees.

senses.definition: To like, prefer, or support one thing more than another.
senses.example: I favor the larger letters because they are easier to read.

senses.definition: The thing or person you like best.
senses.example: Of all the games, the word puzzle is my favorite.

senses.definition: Liked best among a group of people or things.
senses.example: My favorite seat is next to the window.

senses.definition: The feeling you get when you think something bad or dangerous could happen.
senses.example: With practice, my fear of speaking to the group grew smaller.

senses.definition: To feel afraid of something or worry it might happen.
senses.example: I feared we would miss the last train.

senses.definition: A large or special meal, often part of a celebration.
senses.example: We shared a feast after the parade.

senses.definition: To eat and enjoy a large or special meal.
senses.example: We feasted on garden vegetables and warm bread.

senses.definition: An important or noticeable part of something.
senses.example: One feature of the map is a key showing what the symbols mean.

senses.definition: To show or include something as an important part.
senses.example: The exhibit will feature pictures of old trains.

senses.definition: A way of organizing a country so that power is divided between a national government and governments for smaller parts, such as states.
senses.example: Under federalism in the United States, the national government and the states have different jobs and share some responsibilities.

senses.definition: To know what something is like by touching it, or have a sense through your body.
senses.example: Feel the cloth and tell me whether it is rough.

senses.definition: To have an emotion or a sense that something is true.
senses.example: I feel happy about how we worked together.

senses.definition: The way something seems to the touch or when you experience it.
senses.example: I like the smooth feel of the stone.

senses.definition: An upright barrier, often made of boards or wire, that marks or closes in an area.
senses.example: Our rabbit stayed inside the fence.

senses.definition: To build a barrier around or along a place.
senses.example: The gardeners fenced the beds to keep out rabbits.

senses.definition: A way some living things get energy by changing sugars into other substances.
senses.example: During fermentation, tiny gas bubbles appeared in the bread dough.

senses.definition: A small number of things or people.
senses.example: There are a few chairs near the door.

senses.definition: A small number.
senses.example: Many seeds were planted, but only a few grew.

senses.definition: Parts of plant food that your own digestive juices break down only a little or not at all.
senses.example: An apple can provide dietary fiber.

senses.definition: A thin thread of glass or plastic that carries light along it.
senses.example: A small pulse of light can travel a long way inside a fiber optic.

senses.definition: Stories about imagined characters or events, even when some details come from real life.
senses.example: We read a story about a talking spider in the fiction section.

senses.definition: An area of open land, such as land used for crops or sports.
senses.example: We walked across a field of tall grass.

senses.definition: A subject or area of work.
senses.example: Alice studies stars and other objects in the field of astronomy.

senses.definition: In some sports, to catch or stop a ball that has been hit.
senses.example: The player ran to field the ball.

senses.definition: A person’s shape, a drawing, or an important person.
senses.example: A small figure in a red coat appeared at the end of the trail.

senses.definition: A number, often one in a list or calculation.
senses.example: The figure at the bottom shows this week’s total.

senses.definition: To think, work out a number, or understand something.
senses.example: Use the map to figure out which road leads to the bridge.

senses.definition: To understand something or find the answer by thinking about it.
senses.example: We can figure out which key fits by studying their shapes.

senses.definition: A named group of information kept on a computer.
senses.example: I saved my picture as a file.

senses.definition: A short ending after a dot in a filename, often used to show the type of file.
senses.example: The file extension .jpg often shows that a file holds a picture.

senses.definition: To put something into a space until it is full or reaches the needed amount.
senses.example: We used a pitcher to fill the glasses.

senses.definition: To put missing words or information into an empty space.
senses.example: Fill in your team name at the top of the score sheet.

senses.definition: To do someone’s job while that person is away.
senses.example: Our neighbor can fill in as coach on Saturday.

senses.definition: Something that lets some parts of a mixture through and holds other parts back.
senses.example: A paper filter holds back the grains when water drips through.

senses.definition: To remove parts of a mixture by passing it through something.
senses.example: The kidneys filter small materials from the blood.

senses.definition: Getting food by removing tiny living things or other bits from the water as it flows past or through the body.
senses.example: By filter feeding, the mussel gathers food from seawater.

senses.definition: To discover something by looking for it or by chance.
senses.example: I finally found my missing pencil under the book.

senses.definition: To learn the answer or come to think something after trying it.
senses.example: I find that drawing a picture helps me solve the problem.

senses.definition: A thing that someone has discovered or found.
senses.example: The old coin was a lucky find.

senses.definition: To learn information you did not know before.
senses.example: Let’s find out where the creek meets the river.

senses.definition: Good enough or of very good quality.
senses.example: These shoes are fine for the short walk.

senses.definition: Very thin or made of small particles.
senses.example: Fine grains of sand slipped through my fingers.

senses.definition: Money someone must pay for breaking a rule or law.
senses.example: There was a fine for parking in the wrong place.

senses.definition: To require someone to pay money for breaking a rule or law.
senses.example: The town can fine drivers who ignore the parking signs.

senses.definition: One of the long parts at the end of a hand. People often use the word for the four that are not the thumb.
senses.example: I used one finger to point at the picture.

senses.definition: To touch or feel something with the fingers.
senses.example: I fingered the loose thread on the cuff.

senses.definition: To bring something to an end, or to reach the end of it.
senses.example: I need five minutes to finish the picture.

senses.definition: The end of an activity, or the surface look or feel given to an object.
senses.example: We watched the runners reach the finish.

senses.definition: Solid or steady and not easy to bend, move, or change.
senses.example: The trail was firm enough to ride on.

senses.definition: A company or business.
senses.example: My friend’s aunt works for a firm that designs houses.

senses.definition: To be the right size or shape for something, or put something in its proper place.
senses.example: Will this lid fit the jar?

senses.definition: Healthy and strong, or suitable for something.
senses.example: The path is fit for bikes after the repairs.

senses.definition: A sudden spell of doing or feeling something strongly.
senses.example: The joke sent us into a fit of giggles.

senses.definition: To repair something that is broken or solve a problem.
senses.example: We fixed the loose wheel on the cart.

senses.definition: To prepare something to eat or decide a time, price, or rule.
senses.example: I can fix a snack while you set the table.

senses.definition: A long, narrow arm of the sea between steep slopes, formed when seawater filled a valley carved by ice.
senses.example: A boat sailed up a fjord between the steep mountains.

senses.definition: A piece of cloth or a picture used as a sign for a group, country, or instruction.
senses.example: The yellow flag warned us to move slowly.

senses.definition: To mark something so someone will notice it later.
senses.example: Please flag any page with a tricky question.

senses.definition: Even and level, without much bending or height.
senses.example: The table has a flat top.

senses.definition: Having lost most or all of its air or bubbles.
senses.example: The bike tire went flat halfway home.

senses.definition: The particular taste of a food or drink.
senses.example: The soup had a mild onion flavor.

senses.definition: To add taste to a food or drink.
senses.example: We flavored the water with lemon.

senses.definition: A flat limb that helps an animal swim or steer.
senses.example: The sea lion pulled itself forward with its front flippers.

senses.definition: To stay up on or near the surface of a liquid, or move gently through air or water.
senses.example: The empty bowl can float in the tub.

senses.definition: Something that stays on top of water, or a decorated vehicle in a parade.
senses.example: The last float in the parade had a giant paper bee.

senses.definition: Water that covers land that is usually dry.
senses.example: A flood covered the low path near the river.

senses.definition: For water to cover an area or fill a place.
senses.example: Heavy rain can flood low parts of the park.

senses.definition: A fine powder made by grinding grain, beans, or similar foods. People use it in bread and many other foods.
senses.example: We stirred two cups of flour into the bowl.

senses.definition: To dust a surface with this powder, often to stop dough from sticking.
senses.example: Please flour the board before we roll out the dough.

senses.definition: The part of some plants that helps them make seeds. It often has colorful petals.
senses.example: A bee landed on the purple flower.

senses.definition: To grow and open blooms.
senses.example: The tulips flower each spring.

senses.definition: One of the broad sections of a whale’s two-part tail.
senses.example: White marks showed on the humpback whale’s flukes.

senses.definition: To move through the air, with wings, in an aircraft, or in another way.
senses.example: The young birds learned to fly above the garden.

senses.definition: An insect with a single pair of wings. Houseflies, fruit flies, and mosquitoes belong to this group.
senses.example: A fly landed on the window screen.

senses.definition: A trip that takes a spacecraft close past an object so it can observe it.
senses.example: Voyager 2 took pictures during a flyby of Neptune.

senses.definition: An outer arch that carries a push from the upper part of a building out to a strong support on the ground.
senses.example: A flying buttress supported the wall beside a tall window.

senses.definition: The main thing someone is paying attention to.
senses.example: The group’s focus was making the sign easier to read.

senses.definition: To pay close attention or make an image clear.
senses.example: Please focus on the first question.

senses.definition: To bend or lay one part of something over another part.
senses.example: Fold the top of the paper down.

senses.definition: The bend or line made when one part of something is laid over another.
senses.example: Check that the fold lines up with both corners.

senses.definition: A named place that holds files or other folders on a computer.
senses.example: I put both drawings in a folder called Art.

senses.definition: A traditional story people pass from one teller to another over time.
senses.example: My aunt learned that folktale from her grandmother.

senses.definition: A tiny pocket in the body, such as the kind in skin where a hair begins.
senses.example: Each hair starts to grow inside a follicle.

senses.definition: To go behind or after someone or something.
senses.example: We followed the guide to the next room.

senses.definition: To do what a rule or direction says, or understand what is being explained.
senses.example: I can follow the directions on the back of the box.

senses.definition: A path that shows how food and energy pass from one kind of living thing to the next as it eats the one before it.
senses.example: Grass, a rabbit and a fox can make one food chain.

senses.definition: A picture or idea showing who eats whom among many living things in one place.
senses.example: Kelp, sea urchins, and sea otters are connected in a food web.

senses.definition: The part of a person’s or animal’s body at the end of a leg that touches the ground when standing or walking.
senses.example: I balanced on one foot.

senses.definition: A unit of length equal to twelve inches.
senses.example: The ruler was one foot long.

senses.definition: The lowest part or base of something tall.
senses.example: We stopped at the foot of the hill before climbing.

senses.definition: Here is one example of what I mean.
senses.example: We can measure time in different ways. For instance, a sundial uses a shadow.

senses.definition: A push or pull that can change how something moves or change its shape.
senses.example: The force from my hand made the door swing open.

senses.definition: To make someone do something or make something move by using strength or pressure.
senses.example: The wind forced the door shut.

senses.definition: A statement about what is likely to happen, especially with the weather.
senses.example: The forecast says we may get snow tonight.

senses.definition: To predict what is likely to happen.
senses.example: The weather team forecasted rain for the weekend.

senses.definition: The part of a picture that seems closest to the viewer.
senses.example: Tall grass filled the foreground of the landscape.

senses.definition: A large area where many trees grow close enough to shape the land and the life around them.
senses.example: We heard an owl as we walked through the forest.

senses.definition: The layer made by the highest branches and leaves in a forest.
senses.example: The hawk landed above the forest canopy.

senses.definition: The place where a forest meets an open area or a different kind of land.
senses.example: Wild berry bushes grew in bright light by the forest edge.

senses.definition: A dead tree that still stands in the woods.
senses.example: The woodpecker built its nest in a hole in a forest snag.

senses.definition: To stop remembering something or fail to think of it when you need it.
senses.example: I sometimes forget where I put my hat.

senses.definition: To choose to stop blaming someone or holding on to anger about what the person did.
senses.example: I was ready to forgive my friend after we talked.

senses.definition: The shape of something, especially its shape in three dimensions.
senses.example: The clay took the form of a bird.

senses.definition: A great amount of money or valuable things.
senses.example: In the story, the king kept his fortune in a locked room.

senses.definition: Good or bad luck or the way events turn out for someone.
senses.example: We had the good fortune to find a dry place in the storm.

senses.definition: Toward the front, toward a later time, or toward a goal.
senses.example: Please step forward when I call your name.

senses.definition: Facing or moving toward the front.
senses.example: Take one forward step and two steps to the left.

senses.definition: To send something, such as an email, on to another person or place.
senses.example: Can you forward the message to our team?

senses.definition: A part, shape, or trace of a living thing from long ago that was preserved naturally.
senses.example: The footprint in the rock is a kind of fossil.

senses.definition: A way to name a number by telling how many equal parts of a whole you have.
senses.example: The fraction 3/4 means three parts when the whole is divided into four equal parts.

senses.definition: Easy to break or damage, so it needs careful handling.
senses.example: The thin glass ornament was fragile.

senses.definition: One picture in a series that makes a film or animation.
senses.example: We moved the toy a little before taking the next frame.

senses.definition: Able to do what you choose, or able to move without being held.
senses.example: After lunch we are free to choose a game.

senses.definition: Given or available without payment.
senses.example: The library offers free story time.

senses.definition: To let someone go or remove what holds something.
senses.example: We used a stick to free the toy boat from the reeds.

senses.definition: Poetry that can use flexible line lengths without a required pattern of beats or rhymes.
senses.example: His free verse poem paused after the words “wet leaves.”

senses.definition: To change from a liquid to a solid because of cold, or make that happen.
senses.example: We froze grape juice in a tray to make little ice cubes.

senses.definition: To stop moving suddenly and stay still.
senses.example: I froze when I heard a deer step onto the path.

senses.definition: The temperature at which a liquid forms solid crystals under given conditions.
senses.example: Dissolved salt lowered the freezing point of the water.

senses.definition: Happening often.
senses.example: The hikers took frequent rests on the steep path.

senses.definition: Newly made, picked, or prepared.
senses.example: The bread still smelled fresh in the morning.

senses.definition: New or different from what came before.
senses.example: After lunch, we had a fresh idea for our project.

senses.definition: An area where water that is not salty soaks or covers the ground often enough to shape what lives there.
senses.example: Water stood in the freshwater wetland long after the field dried.

senses.definition: One of the thin bars across the neck of a guitar or similar instrument, used to guide where a string stops vibrating.
senses.example: She pressed the string just behind the third fret.

senses.definition: A force that acts between touching surfaces to resist sliding, or that can stop them from starting to slide.
senses.example: Friction between the tires and the road helped the bicycle turn.

senses.definition: A person you know, like, and enjoy spending time with.
senses.example: My friend and I read the same book.

senses.definition: Kind and easy to get along with.
senses.example: A friendly neighbor helped me carry the box.

senses.definition: To make someone or something feel afraid.
senses.example: A sudden shout can frighten a cat.

senses.definition: The side that faces forward, or the leading part of something.
senses.example: I stood at the front of the line.

senses.definition: At or near the side facing forward.
senses.example: I left my shoes by the front door.

senses.definition: The boundary between two large bodies of air with different conditions.
senses.example: A cold front brought rain overnight.

senses.definition: To pull your eyebrows together or turn your mouth down to show worry, dislike, or deep thought.
senses.example: I frowned when I saw the torn page.

senses.definition: An expression made by pulling your eyebrows together or turning the corners of your mouth down.
senses.example: Her frown showed she was puzzled.

senses.definition: The part that develops from a flowering plant’s ovary and usually contains seeds.
senses.example: A cucumber is a fruit even when you use it in a salad.

senses.definition: The point that a lever turns around.
senses.example: The support under the middle of a seesaw is its fulcrum.

senses.definition: Enjoyment or something that gives you pleasure.
senses.example: We had fun playing cards on the porch.

senses.definition: Enjoyable or entertaining.
senses.example: Our class made a fun game out of the spelling practice.

senses.definition: In programming, a group of steps a program can use as one unit, often by calling it by name.
senses.example: One function draws a star where the player taps.

senses.definition: An amount of money set aside for a particular purpose.
senses.example: Our club started a fund to buy art supplies.

senses.definition: To provide money to pay for something.
senses.example: The school will fund the new reading program.

senses.definition: A living thing such as a mushroom, mold or yeast that gets food by absorbing it from other material.
senses.example: The fungus absorbed food from a fallen log.

senses.definition: Making people laugh.
senses.example: My cousin told a funny story.

senses.definition: Odd or hard to explain.
senses.example: I heard a funny little noise under the steps.

senses.definition: Movable things such as chairs, beds, and tables that people use in a room.
senses.example: The only furniture in my room is a bed, a desk, and a chair.

senses.definition: The time after the present.
senses.example: Who will use this park in the future?

senses.definition: Expected to happen, exist, or be used later.
senses.example: We kept the extra seeds for a future garden.
